name: Photonic Stress Fracture Pistol PSFP-3 'Cleaver'
description:
The Photonic Stress Fracture Pistol PSFP-3 operates on the principle of photoinduced thermal stress — it fires a rapid-pulse infrared laser that heats the surface of a target material faster than the underlying structure can dissipate the energy, creating a steep thermal gradient that induces mechanical fracture along the material's weakest internal lines. Against inorganic targets such as ceramics, composites, and hardened cyberware housing, this produces catastrophic surface cracking and structural failure. Against biological tissue, the effect is a deep, clean laceration as surface cells flash-expand and rupture in a line determined by the beam path.

Helix Biosystems developed the PSFP-3 as a surgical tool before its obvious weapons applications were licensed to civilian security markets. The 'Cleaver' designation emerged from field use — unlike burn weapons, it doesn't char or cauterize, it simply splits. The beam pulse duration is short enough that coagulation is minimal, meaning wounds bleed freely and healing is complicated. Surgeons who work in GLMZ's trauma wards have a particular hatred for it. The weapon leaves entry wounds that look almost decorative in their precision, which has made it a calling card for certain operators who want their work recognized.

The PSFP-3's distinctive aesthetic is a narrow, matte-black frame with a deep violet indicator light that pulses once before each shot — a safety feature from its surgical origins that became impossible to remove without voiding the power regulation system. Experienced targets have learned to treat that violet pulse as a last warning. In enclosed spaces, the weapon produces a faint crackling sound as materials fracture, which some operators find deeply satisfying and others find unbearable.
legality: Licensed — medical and security use; Restricted — general civilian
specifications: effective range: 2–30 meters beam pulse duration: 0.8 milliseconds per shot thermal gradient output: 420°C surface differential per pulse power source: Compact photonic cell, 60 shots per charge weight: 0.9 kg anti-materiel rating: Grade 3 ceramic and composite surfaces biological wound profile: Clean laceration, minimal cauterization, high bleed rate form factor: Compact sidearm, single-hand operation
tactical_use: Used in close- to mid-range engagements where precision is prioritized over area effect. Effective against armored targets by targeting joint seams and sensor housings rather than armored faces directly — the fracture propagates along stress lines the operator cannot see but the weapon's targeting assist estimates from surface geometry. In anti-personnel use, operators favor torso and limb shots that maximize blood loss over immediately incapacitating head shots, creating sustained pressure on medical support resources. Often used as a secondary weapon by operators who prefer to disable before finishing.
cultural_context: The PSFP-3 occupies an uncomfortable space in GLMZ's weapons culture — it was born in a hospital and carries that clinical precision into violence. Carrying one marks a person as either medically trained, deeply methodical, or both. In the city's underground surgery community, it's both despised and respected: despised because the wounds it creates are difficult and expensive to repair, respected because using one requires genuine understanding of material and biological structure. Some high-end assassins use it specifically because the wounds it leaves are attributed to surgical skill, implying a message beyond the act of killing.
known_users: HELIX BIOSYSTEMS licensed surgical security teams
Underground surgeons who have crossed into violence
'Scalpel' — an assassin whose signature is wounds that look like surgical errors
Corporate espionage agents targeting cyberware implants for extraction
story_hooks: A series of murders in the medical district have been committed with a PSFP-3 calibrated to replicate botched surgical complications — someone is killing people and making it look like malpractice.

A stolen shipment of PSFP-3s with modified pulse durations that prevent any wound coagulation at all has made it onto the market — the modifications are signed with a HELIX internal engineer's credentials.

A player character is hired to recover a PSFP-3 used in a high-profile killing, but the weapon has been modified to record biometric data on every target it wounds — a database of victims that someone very powerful wants buried.

A street medic has begun using a PSFP-3 for emergency field surgery in the lower districts — technically illegal but saving lives — and the licensing authority wants them arrested while the community wants them protected.
related_entities: Carrion Defense Works Field Surgical Kit FSK-6

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, minimalist sidearm with an almost surgical precision to its lines. The frame tapers from a slightly wider grip to a narrow, almost pen-like barrel assembly. The overall impression is of refined lethality — less brutal instrument, more engineered scalpel. Sits low and compact in the hand.
physical_description.dimensions: Length: 18.5 cm | Width: 4.2 cm | Height: 12 cm (grip to top of slide) | Barrel length: 8.3 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively light — 0.9 kg feels almost insubstantial until you realize the photonic cell and targeting assembly account for most of that mass. Balanced toward the grip, making it feel like an extension of the hand rather than a tool being wielded.
physical_description.primary_material: Carbon-composite polymer frame with reinforced titanium alloy slide and barrel assembly. The photonic emitter housing is aerospace-grade ceramic to withstand thermal cycling.
physical_description.finish: Matte black throughout — not the aggressive black of military hardware, but the clinical black of surgical instruments. The finish has a slight satin quality that prevents glare.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: Deep matte black | Accent: Violet (the indicator light housing and minimal trim around the emitter aperture)
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer with fine cross-hatching — mimics medical-grade glove grip patterns from its surgical heritage. Slightly textured, not aggressive, designed for precision rather than purchase.
distinctive_features: Deep violet indicator light positioned above the trigger guard that pulses once before each shot
Circular aperture for photonic emission, smaller than typical laser weapons — almost innocuously small
Minimal control surface — trigger, safety lever, and charge status indicator. No visible rails or attachment points
Heat vents along the grip frame in a subtle geometric pattern, barely visible
Target-assist laser sight integrated into the top — appears as a thin crimson line when active
Photonic cell housing visible as a slight bulge in the grip, with faint status LEDs (green/yellow/red) along the spine
Serial plate etched subtly into the left side of the frame in small type
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: HELIX BIOSYSTEMS logo (interlocking DNA helix) etched in chrome on the right side of the slide, about 2 cm from the rear. Tiny 'PSFP-3' designation stamped below it. Serial number on left frame spine. 'CLEAVER' designation is not official — it's user-applied by field operators, sometimes as custom engravings.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained in standard field use — the matte finish shows micro-wear patterns from holster draw and handling, but the weapon is typically kept clean. The photonic emitter aperture remains pristine due to self-cleaning thermal pulses. In heavy-use conditions, faint scorch marks may appear around the emitter housing from ambient material fracturing.
